item.title: ‘End game’: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce mocked by opponent
item.description: Feb 11, 2024; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Recording artist Taylor Swift reacts during the first quarter of Super Bowl LVIII between Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Seattle Seahawks handed the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss of the season on Sunday night, and they made sure to rub it in afterward by trolling newlyweds Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift. After their 20-3 win on Sunday Night Football , the Seahawks posted a Swift-themed troll on social media, sharing a friendship bracelet that spelled out “Seahawks Win.” And for the caption, they went with the title of one of Swift’s songs. Seahawks Dominate Chiefs Kansas City entered the night as one of the NFL’s last two undefeated teams, but Seattle’s defense shut the Chiefs down. Kansas City managed just 213 total yards and 11 first downs, and went 3-of-11 on third down in the 20-3 loss. Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards and an interception, and the Chiefs failed to reach the red zone for the first time in a game with Mahomes as their starting quarterback, according to Pro Football Talk . Kansas City’s three points were the fewest in a Mahomes start since 2021. Meanwhile, Jaxon Smith-Njigba torched the Chiefs’ secondary for nine catches, 150 yards, and a touchdown. Kelce got off to a slow start, failing to catch a pass in the first half. However, he finished the game with four catches for 44 yards, and moved into fifth place on the NFL’s all-time receptions list. With the loss, Kansas City fell to 5-1, leaving the Minnesota Vikings as the NFL’s only undefeated team. ‘End Game’ After the game, the Seahawks wasted no time in trolling Swift and Kelce as the team’s official account posted a photo of a friendship bracelet reading “Seahawks Win.” The caption simply read, “End Game,” a reference to a song from Swift’s 2017 album reputation . End Game https://t.co/fUGMpcCMjX — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026 The bracelet is a nod to a tradition among Swift’s fans, who made and traded friendship bracelets at her Eras Tour concerts. It’s also a nod to how Swift and Kelce got together. Kelce attended one of Swift’s shows in July 2023 and tried to give her a bracelet with his number on it, as ESPN noted . He wasn’t able to deliver it, but the two started dating a couple of months later, and they got married this past July. Needless to say, Chiefs fans and Swifties probably didn’t find the joke very funny. The post ‘End game’: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce mocked by opponent appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: St. John’s men’s basketball wrangles Texas in encouraging exhibition finale
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; New York, NY, USA; St. John's Red Storm guard Tounde Yessoufou (24) gestures after making a three point shot in the first half against the Texas Longhorns at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Although St. John’s survived last week’s four-overtime gauntlet against Rutgers with a win, they were unsatisfied with their performance and knew they needed to take massive strides to contend with seventh-ranked Texas in their final tune-up. They not only met the challenge, but also overdelivered. The Red Storm ended their preseason on a high note with an 87-74 wire-to-wire win over the Longhorns on Sunday afternoon, proving they can outmatch the country’s best when their game clicks. “I felt that we had to make a quantum leap from the Rutgers game,” Rick Pitino said on Sunday, “I was on them constantly on certain things, and they made a quantum leap today.” St. John’s set the tone with active defense, turning ten Texas first-half turnovers into 14 points and holding the Longhorns to just 42.3% shooting before halftime. The Red Storm took the lead on a Tounde Yessoufou steal and breakaway layup at the 19:07 mark in the first half, and they held onto it for the remainder of the contest. Tounde with the steal and score early 🔥 pic.twitter.com/9JN9RNTj66 — St. John's Men’s Basketball (@StJohnsBBall) October 25, 2026 Yessoufou, along with Ian Jackson and Keyshawn Hall, overwhelmed the Longhorns all day long. The offensively gifted trio showed off their firepower, scoring 65 of the Red Storm’s 87 total points and shooting 23-of-41 from the field (56 percent), and they shut down a Texas rally going into halftime by combining for a 12-0 run to send St. John’s into the break with a 49-31 lead. That margin ballooned to 22 points early in the second half. “Every game is important to us; we want to show we can be connected, and today our play showed for itself,” Tounde Yessoufou told the media after the game. The Baylor transfer showcased his two-way skill set with 23 points (8-of-14), five assists, and five steals, attacking the basket with authority and flexing his range with two made triples. Tounde Yessoufou is an absolute DOG pic.twitter.com/YSp8lJ4W7A — Cole Adams (@coleadamss) October 25, 2026 Ian Jackson put behind shoddy outings in the Red Storm’s previous two scrimmages and played with all sorts of control on Sunday, scoring 18 points (7-of-14), leading the Johnnies with three made triples, giving four assists, and hitting the glass for six rebounds, the second most of any Red Storm player. item.title: Broncos are home underdogs to Chiefs in Week 8 (OVERDOG SZN)
item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs is tackled by the Denver Broncos during the first half of an NFL football game at Empower Field at Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos needed the Kansas City Chiefs to stumble in order to catch them and stumbled they did on the road on Sunday Night Football being dominated by the Seattle Seahawks to fall to 5-1. That means the winner of next week’s game will be in first place in the AFC West. Denver has a real chance to get revenge for the Week 1 massacre and silence some of those doubters. According to FanDuel , the Broncos are 1.5-point home underdogs against the Chiefs in Week 8. The over/under stands at 41.5 for this matchup. Broncos vs. Chiefs betting odds Denver Broncos vs. Kansas City Chiefs Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 2:25 P.M. Mile High time Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado ATS Betting Lines: Kansas City -1.5 Moneyline Odds: Denver +102 / Kansas City -12- Over/Under: 41.5 Broncos Country, ride with us on the SB Nation app! Follow the action and experience every game alongside a community of passionate Broncos fans. Join the live game-day conversation Enjoy fewer ads Easily jump between communities Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . For the Broncos offense, they have to play like they did last week — obviously — and avoid the three-and-out issue. They largely did that on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. However, in Week 1 they did not. It would be good to see Denver stick with Jonah Coleman in this game. He seemed to have must better vision than J.K. Dobbins last week, but I’m also okay to stick with a hot hand if someone has one against the Chiefs. Defensively, they have got to contain Kenneth Walker III. We saw what happened when he gets completely shut down like he was against the Seahawks. The Chiefs offense only scored three points and Patrick Mahomes looked pedestrian. Denver’s defense has come a long way since Week 1 and I hope they learned some valuable lessons from that game. If they come out and shut KW3 down, then this game should break the Broncos way. What are your predictions for the Broncos-Chiefs game in Week 8?

item.title: Kane primed to pip Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d'Or glory
item.description: Harry Kane is the favourite to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday (Joe Klamar) England captain Harry Kane is the favourite to win a wide open race to be crowned Ballon d'Or winner at a glitzy London ceremony on Monday, with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe also in the running to be named the world's best footballer. The 70th edition of the award, established by the magazine France Football, will be hosted in England for the first time in recognition of the first winner Stanley Matthews and fittingly could have a first English winner for 25 years. Bayern Munich striker Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, leading the German giants to a league and cup double and England to the semi-finals of the World Cup. "I'd love to be able to achieve something like that. I would be a massive milestone in my career," said the 33-year-old. But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and World Cup for Kane means the outcome is far from certain. "I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone," he added. "I can see why they don't tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names, and there will be more people watching it if they don't know." - 'I deserve it' - Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain's Ousmane Dembele last year and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d'Or winner one day. However, after a hamstring injury ended his club season early, he was far from the shining light of Spain's World Cup triumph that was built on being the best collective unit. Yamal was pipped to both the player and young player of the tournament by his Barcelona team-mates Rodri and Pau Cubarsi. That has not diminished his bullish confidence ahead of the ceremony. "For me, Mbappe and me, we're the two best players in the world," Yamal said last month. "I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I've won." Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France. The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies. His 10 World Cup goals made him the top goalscorer in the competition's history on 22. "Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out," said Mbappe. "Who am I voting for? Myself." One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA's rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist, allocating a maximum of 15 points down to one based on their ranking. The Ballon d'Or goes to the player who accrued the most points. Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners as well as increasing a player's overall mark

Putellas, winner in 2021 and 2022, was part of the Barcelona side that regained the Champions League last season before moving to London City Lionesses. Her former club team-mate, Poland's Ewa Pajor is the main challenger to Putellas after she netted 11 Champions League goals in Barca's latest triumph. kca/pb

item.title: Seahawks' all Studs and no Duds in Week 7 statement win over Chiefs
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday Night Football, sending a statement to the rest of the NFL. The Chiefs came in undefeated at 5-0, while the Seahawks had plenty to prove at 3-3. What’s underrated is that Seattle just played the two most physical teams in the league in a five-day span last week, while Kansas City has been beating up on largely inferior opponents. There were too many honorable mentions to list them all in this performance, but linebacker Tyrice Knight deserves a mention for stepping in for an injured Drake Thomas and fitting his gaps well, and tight end AJ Barner was an excellent Robin to Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s Batman in the passing game. We’ll discuss more individual performances as we evaluate the film this week. Without further ado, here are your six Studs and zero Duds for Week 7. STUDS Nick Emmanwori Nick Emmanwori didn’t fill up the stat sheet tonight — he allowed his teammates to do so, while making sure the Chiefs didn’t. Every time they showed him on a replay, he was making a game-changing play or terrifying Kansas City’s offense when they tried to establish a rhythm. Two coverage reps on NFL Scouting Combine 40-yard dash record holder and Chiefs wide receiver Xavier Worthy showed Emmanwori clamping him, going stride-for-stride on a slot fade and keeping him blanketed on a crosser. Team leader Smith-Njigba took the podium to begin the postgame press conference and called him “the most versatile player in the league.” Emmanwori’s magnum opus of the night, though, was his chasedown of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, which caused him to throw an uncharacteristically terrible pass that ended up in the hands of fellow safety Ty Okada for an interception. Safety, linebacker, defensive end — whatever position Nick Emmanwori plays, he instills fear in the opponent. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (JSN) There were murmurs of Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane playing man coverage on JSN this week, and Kansas City was forced to try it early. It ended the same way it does for every other defensive back — two explosive receptions that threw a wrench in the gameplan before the first half was over. JSN had nine receptions on 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown, keeping him first among NFL wideouts in all three categories. He lined up inside and outside as a modern receiver should tonight, ran all sorts of routes, and kept finding his way down the middle of the field and the sideline. Fellow Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp handed him the baton of the modern receiving prototype when he came to Seattle, and JSN’s run farther than anyone could’ve imagined with it to define the position’s evolution in the last decade. item.content:encoded: The Seattle Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday Night Football, sending a statement to the rest of the NFL. The Chiefs came in undefeated at 5-0, while the Seahawks had plenty to prove at 3-3. What’s underrated is that Seattle just played the two most physical teams in the league in a five-day span last week, while Kansas City has been beating up on largely inferior opponents. There were too many honorable mentions to list them all in this performance, but linebacker Tyrice Knight deserves a mention for stepping in for an injured Drake Thomas and fitting his gaps well, and tight end AJ Barner was an excellent Robin to Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s Batman in the passing game. We’ll discuss more individual performances as we evaluate the film this week. Without further ado, here are your six Studs and zero Duds for Week 7. STUDS Nick Emmanwori Nick Emmanwori didn’t fill up the stat sheet tonight — he allowed his teammates to do so, while making sure the Chiefs didn’t. Every time they showed him on a replay, he was making a game-changing play or terrifying Kansas City’s offense when they tried to establish a rhythm. Two coverage reps on NFL Scouting Combine 40-yard dash record holder and Chiefs wide receiver Xavier Worthy showed Emmanwori clamping him, going stride-for-stride on a slot fade and keeping him blanketed on a crosser. Team leader Smith-Njigba took the podium to begin the postgame press conference and called him “the most versatile player in the league.” Emmanwori’s magnum opus of the night, though, was his chasedown of Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, which caused him to throw an uncharacteristically terrible pass that ended up in the hands of fellow safety Ty Okada for an interception. Safety, linebacker, defensive end — whatever position Nick Emmanwori plays, he instills fear in the opponent. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (JSN) There were murmurs of Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane playing man coverage on JSN this week, and Kansas City was forced to try it early. It ended the same way it does for every other defensive back — two explosive receptions that threw a wrench in the gameplan before the first half was over. JSN had nine receptions on 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown, keeping him first among NFL wideouts in all three categories. He lined up inside and outside as a modern receiver should tonight, ran all sorts of routes, and kept finding his way down the middle of the field and the sideline. Fellow Seahawks wide receiver Cooper Kupp handed him the baton of the modern receiving prototype when he came to Seattle, and JSN’s run farther than anyone could’ve imagined with it to define the position’s evolution in the last decade. Emanuel Wilson No position group on the Seahawks has had more consistent struggles than their running back room, but Emanuel Wilson quelled the doubts tonight. He became the team’s first 100-yard rusher of the season tonight on 24 carries, and showed a surprising improvement in vision that even Kenneth Walker III struggled with. He outplayed his counterpart on the Chiefs after a week chock-full of media hype around the Super Bowl LX MVP, and although his style isn’t typically explosive, he’s a consistently tough grinder. He’ll still have a role when Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price eventually return because of this. Anthony Bradford Right guards never get the glory they deserve, but Anthony Bradford had one of the best offensive line performances the Seahawks have seen this season in Week 7. It showed up individually as he used his sheer strength to manhandle Chiefs defenders into the ground. It showed up far more in the entire unit’s improvement, though, as they were able to run the football effectively and kept quarterback Sam Darnold as clean as any game this season despite going against a tough Kansas City defensive line. Bradford was thought to be replaceable last season, but 2026 has been an examination of his value in a way few could’ve foreseen. Seahawks Defensive Line The story of the night was Super Bowl LX MVP and former Seahawks running back Kenneth Walker III returning to face his old team, while having one of the best seasons for a running back in NFL history through five games. It appears the Seahawks hold the keys to Walker, because their defensive line made him a complete non-factor to the point Kansas City stopped using him altogether. They ran up the stat sheet while displaying their trademark violence in a way no other team is able to do. While some thought their 35-game streak of not allowing a 100-yard rusher was in jeopardy tonight, they extended it to 36 against the NFL’s leading rusher coming into this week. Defensive tackles Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy II both need to be considered for All-Pro nods, while the edge presence of Derick Hall, Demarcus Lawrence and Uchenna Nwosu gives them as clear an identity as you can imagine. Ty Okada It’s easy to forget about safety Ty Okada when his game-changing play happened early in the game, but his opportunistic nature was just what the doctor ordered for this secondary. He hasn’t had a chance to shine since coming back for the team’s two recent losses to the Denver Broncos and San Francisco 49ers, but made sure he would when he popped up in the right spot to intercept Mahomes’ pressured throw, playing the complementary football Emmanwori needed when wreaking havoc in the backfield. The Seahawks' momentum was mounting before this, but it felt like that was the moment they turned the game into their practice field. Follow seahawkswire.usatoday.com and @TheSeahawksWire on X for human analysis of all things Seahawks. item.title: 76ers star Tyrese Maxey speaks up on situation that led to LeBron James starting at center
item.description: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images 76ers star Tyrese Maxey speaks up on situation that led to LeBron James starting at center appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Tyrese Maxey and the Philadelphia 76ers have been getting creative with a short-handed frontcourt , even sliding LeBron James to center. After Sunday’s loss, Maxey made it clear the team would welcome some reinforcements. “If some of our tall guys could come back, that would be great,” he said after the game . The 76ers fell 106-93 to the Detroit Pistons at Xfinity Mobile Arena, suffering their first loss of the season and dropping to 3-1. With the roster thinned out, head coach Nick Nurse started James at center alongside Maxey, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It marked the first time since the 2021-22 season that James started a game at center. Nurse said before tipoff that he thought James was “fine there.” The lineup was largely a product of necessity. Joel Embiid sat out the second night of a back-to-back as part of the team’s long-term plan to manage his right plantar fasciitis, even though he said he felt good enough to play. He was coming off a 28-point, 11-rebound, 10-assist triple-double in Saturday’s win over the Milwaukee Bucks. The rest of the injury report did Philadelphia no favors . Tacko Fall was out with a left quad strain, while forwards Jabari Walker and Dominick Barlow were also sidelined. VJ Edgecombe missed the game with an abdominal contusion. Nurse noted the injury report was filled with “fours and fives,” leaving him with few options in the middle. Philadelphia paid for it early. Detroit raced out to a 25-7 lead and took a 56-44 advantage into halftime. The 76ers clawed back from a 21-point deficit to get within four, but they never got over the hump. Maxey led the way with 29 points despite picking up two early fouls. James added 18 points and five assists in his return from back management, while Brown struggled to a 5-of-20 night for 16 points. Adem Bona gave the 76ers a lift inside with six points and 13 rebounds in 24 minutes. Cade Cunningham paced the Pistons with 26 points. James, 41, has shown he can hold his own at center in a pinch, but it is not a role Philadelphia wants him playing every night. Until Embiid is back and the rest of the frontcourt gets healthy, Maxey and the 76ers will have to keep finding ways to make it work. Related: LeBron James hilariously uses old Taurean Prince quote to address 76ers’ problems Related: Nick Nurse gives Adem Bona his flowers despite 76ers’ loss to Pistons

item.title: Club America lose 1-2 to Pachuca in a poor showing at home
item.description: MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - OCTOBER 25: Oussama Idrissi of Pachuca celebrates after scoring the team's second goal during the Liga MX Torneo Apertura 2026 14th-round match between America and Pachuca at Banorte Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tonight was supposed to be a night of celebration in honor of Club América legend Guillermo ‘Memo’ Ochoa. Instead the Aguilas suffered their second defeat of the season at the hands of Pachuca who were the better team. Now the Aguilas will have to regroup quickly for a weekday game against Tijuana meanwhile Pachuca get a full week of rest when they face Tigres on Saturday. América attempted to get things going quickly as they had their first chance of the night within the first minute of the game. Kevin Alvarez attempted a shot at goal on the right side but his shot went wide. A few minutes later they got another chance at goal as Oscar Perea took his shot but it also went wide. Pachuca did not receive their first shot of the game until the seventh minute when Salomon Rondon made his way into the box but he fouled Santiago Ramos on the way and his chance ended very quickly. Two minutes later the visitors got their second chance as Oussama Idrissi earned a corner for his team but that went nowhere after multiple attempts to get past the América defense. The visitors finally succeeded in the 12th minute after a mistake in the home teams’ defense. Erick ‘Chiquito’ Sanchez made his way back to help defend but he mistakenly passed the ball to his opponents as Alan Bautista received the ball and sent it towards goal and past the outstretched arms of Luis Angel Malagon. ¡La 'Pantera' sacó la magia! 💥 Alan Bautista firmó un GOLAZO con un brillante disparo de larga distancia para adelantar a @Tuzos ante el América. 🚀 #J14 #AP26 ✨ #LaLigaDeLaAfición pic.twitter.com/F2AdSmFG5E — Liga BBVA MX (@LigaBBVAMX) October 26, 2026 The Aguilas attempted to respond immediately but any chance they had in the box they were immediately surrounded by white jerseys. Then it seemed as if the night was going to go from bad to worse for the Aguilas after Pachuca was awarded a penalty after Malagon hit a Tuzos player in the head. Right away the referee was called to VAR to take a closer look at the play. The replay showed multiple things at once: Malagon clashing with a white jersey, Santiago Bueno pulling a white jersey and Carlos Alvarez covering his mouth while talking with an opponent. Let’s not forget that in Liga MX that movement is illegal and punished with a red card. When the referee was finished at the monitor, he announced that there was no penalty and to move on. Surprisingly, the referee did not eject Alvarez even though it was clear he covered his mouth while speaking to a rival. América was saved. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tonight was supposed to be a night of celebration in honor of Club América legend Guillermo ‘Memo’ Ochoa. Instead the Aguilas suffered their second defeat of the season at the hands of Pachuca who were the better team. Now the Aguilas will have to regroup quickly for a weekday game against Tijuana meanwhile Pachuca get a full week of rest when they face Tigres on Saturday. América attempted to get things going quickly as they had their first chance of the night within the first minute of the game. Kevin Alvarez attempted a shot at goal on the right side but his shot went wide. A few minutes later they got another chance at goal as Oscar Perea took his shot but it also went wide. Pachuca did not receive their first shot of the game until the seventh minute when Salomon Rondon made his way into the box but he fouled Santiago Ramos on the way and his chance ended very quickly. Two minutes later the visitors got their second chance as Oussama Idrissi earned a corner for his team but that went nowhere after multiple attempts to get past the América defense. The visitors finally succeeded in the 12th minute after a mistake in the home teams’ defense. Erick ‘Chiquito’ Sanchez made his way back to help defend but he mistakenly passed the ball to his opponents as Alan Bautista received the ball and sent it towards goal and past the outstretched arms of Luis Angel Malagon. ¡La 'Pantera' sacó la magia! 💥 Alan Bautista firmó un GOLAZO con un brillante disparo de larga distancia para adelantar a @Tuzos ante el América. 🚀 #J14 #AP26 ✨ #LaLigaDeLaAfición pic.twitter.com/F2AdSmFG5E — Liga BBVA MX (@LigaBBVAMX) October 26, 2026 The Aguilas attempted to respond immediately but any chance they had in the box they were immediately surrounded by white jerseys. Then it seemed as if the night was going to go from bad to worse for the Aguilas after Pachuca was awarded a penalty after Malagon hit a Tuzos player in the head. Right away the referee was called to VAR to take a closer look at the play. The replay showed multiple things at once: Malagon clashing with a white jersey, Santiago Bueno pulling a white jersey and Carlos Alvarez covering his mouth while talking with an opponent. Let’s not forget that in Liga MX that movement is illegal and punished with a red card. When the referee was finished at the monitor, he announced that there was no penalty and to move on. Surprisingly, the referee did not eject Alvarez even though it was clear he covered his mouth while speaking to a rival. América was saved. The rest of the half went by quickly with Pachuca gaining more confidence attempting to double their lead while the Aguilas were just waiting for the end of the half. The second half started quickly as América was able to level the game just 30 seconds into the second half. Brian Rodriguez started the play on the left side as he then passed the ball to Sanchez who crossed it to the other side of the box where Henry Martin was there to hit the ball into the back of the net with his chest. Sergio Barreto was on that side but he was too focused on the ball and he was unaware of Martin behind him which allowed the striker to score his eighth goal of the season. ¡Las Águilas retoman el vuelo! 🦅 Apenas comenzaba el segundo tiempo cuando Henry Martín apareció para marcar el empate del @ClubAmerica ante Pachuca. 🔥 #J14 #AP26 ✨ #LaLigaDeLaAfición pic.twitter.com/f5Zq2h4dua — Liga BBVA MX (@LigaBBVAMX) October 26, 2026 This goal helped the Aguilas gain confidence and it showed as they were making threatening attacks in Pachuca’s box that either the defense or the goalkeeper Carlos Moreno saved. It wasn’t until the 68th minute that the visitors made their first substitution of the night. Rodolfo Pizarro came off for Mauricio Isais and it was evident that Pizarro was upset with his substitution. However, this change made sense as Pizarro had not had the best night and Benjamin Mora was doing what was best for the team as he was looking for the breakaway goal. That goal came just six minutes later thanks to the linkup between Rondon and Idrissi. Rondon made his way to the top of the box as he drew multiple yellow jerseys towards him which allowed Idrissi to come up unmarked and shoot the ball towards goal and into the back of the net to retake the lead. ¡Idrissi se mandó un GOLAZO! 💥 Ossama Idrissi sacó la magia para devolverle la ventaja a los @Tuzos ante el América. 🧙‍♂️ ¡Una joya! 🔥 #J14 #AP26 ✨ #LaLigaDeLaAfición pic.twitter.com/eGOuFmAZfP — Liga BBVA MX (@LigaBBVAMX) October 26, 2026 After this goal América attempted to draw the game but they had a difficult time doing so as they were swarmed with white jerseys when they made their way inside the box. The home side was visibly frustrated as they tried and tried again to score a goal but they were just not on target in front of goal. It seemed as if their weekday match against Atlas tired them out because the shots they missed were shots they would usually make in any other game. In the 90th minute Miguel Borja had a golden opportunity in front of goal as he was unmarked in front of an open net but he was unable to get his foot on the ball and into the net. Then in the final minute of stoppage time they had another golden opportunity when Rodriguez was fouled right outside of the box. Rodriguez himself stepped up to take the free-kick as it was his specialty. The player took the shot directly at goal but Moreno punched the ball out for a corner. Even with one final chance the Aguilas were unable to do any damage and the game ended immediately after their corner was taken as they suffered just their loss of the season. So far this season América does not have the best record at home since the Estadio Azteca turned into the Estadio Bonarte. So far they have only won three games at home compared to six wins on the road. While this loss hurts, the Aguilas continue to remain at the top of the table with one game in hand and they will have to regroup quickly as they will face the Xolos on the road on Wednesday.

item.title: What Zac Taylor told Bengals in postgame speech after rout of Ravens
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor delivered a memorable postgame speech after the team's NFL Week 7 rout of the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. "Last night we said we're coming on the road for a divisional win to set the momentum for the rest of the season," Taylor said in the locker room . "You guys did exactly that. Couldn't be prouder of you guys. We started a little slow today, but you finished as strong as you could have possibly finished. 35-0 in the second half. Five possessions on offense, five touchdowns. Six possessions on defense, no points." Taylor then proceeded to shout-out several players for their efforts. "I saw Ja'Marr go 5 (catches) for 62 (yards) with the touchdown and a great halftime speech ," Taylor continued. "I saw Tee have his 17th 100-yard game. I saw Joe go 16-of-18 for 249 and four touchdowns. We go home. We play in front of our fans against Tennessee. We got to have a great week of work. We can't afford to waste one second with this momentum we got." The team followed Taylor's speech with a "Who-Dey" chant. With the victory, Taylor passed Bengals founder and Hall of Fame coach Paul Brown, the father of team president and owner Mike Brown, in regular-season wins. The Bengals became just the 10th team in NFL history to get shut out in the first half and then score 35 points or more in the second half, per CBS Sports research. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: What Zac Taylor told Bengals in postgame speech after rout of Ravens

item.title: Knicks HC Mike Brown gets 100% real about decision to cut player for Dalton Knecht
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Knicks HC Mike Brown gets 100% real about decision to cut player for Dalton Knecht appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Dalton Knecht has received a fresh opportunity to revive his NBA career after parting ways with the Los Angeles Lakers. The New York Knicks have agreed to a two-way contract with the former Lakers forward , waiving Kevin McCullar Jr. to make room for him. Knicks head coach Mike Brown is hoping the team’s gamble on the former first-round pick will pay off. Following the Knicks’ 111-102 loss to the Orlando Magic on Sunday, Brown addressed the decision to waive McCullar Jr. to accommodate Knecht. “It wasn’t anything that Kevin didn’t do; he was great,” Brown said. “It was more so having the opportunity to bring a guy like Dalton on just to get to know him a little bit better.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Knecht entered the NBA with high expectations after the Lakers selected him with the 17th overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. The former Tennessee standout averaged 9.1 points and 2.8 rebounds per game across 78 appearances during his rookie season. However, his production declined considerably during his second season. Knecht averaged just 4.2 points and 1.4 rebounds across 54 games during the 2025-26 season, playing approximately 10.2 minutes per game. Now, Knecht’s move to New York gives him a chance to rebuild his confidence and prove he can become a consistent contributor at the NBA level. The former Lakers forward also believes that joining the Knicks is the right move for his career. “It just felt like the best opportunity,” Knecht said. “I talked to the coaching staff, knew them for a while, so it was good. Thought this would be a great fit, and I’m excited to be here.” Meanwhile, things have not gone according to plan for the Knicks, who entered the season as the defending NBA champions. Sunday’s defeat dropped them to 0-3. The Knicks will now look to turn things around quickly and hope their gamble on Knecht pays off. Related: Mike Brown gets brutally honest as Knicks’ winless streak continues after loss to Magic Related: Knicks match troubling trend last seen in 2011 after loss to Magic

item.title: Stephanie Vaquer Returns And The Final Pieces Ahead Of Crown Jewel Come Together
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Lucien Price in action against Jimmy Uso during Monday Night RAW at Pechanga Arena on October 19, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Georgiana Dallas/WWE via Getty Images) WWE via Getty Images WWE’s calendar is rolling toward Crown Jewel on November 7 and Monday’s episode of Raw figures to deliver a few details that will affect the card. We know Stephanie Vaquer is returning to take on Becky Lynch in a No. 1 contender’s match for Liv Morgan ’s WWE Women’s World Championship and we’ve also learned about a few others. From the looks of things, it seems like the ladies will play major roles in this week’s episode of Raw. Let’s talk WWE. WWE Raw Oct. 26 Key Facts Detail Info Date Monday, Oct. 26, 2026 Start time 8 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PT Venue Save Mart Center, Fresno, California Streaming Netflix Next premium live event Crown Jewel, Saturday, Nov. 7 Vaquer has been sidelined since Money in the Bank, where she suffered an ankle injury in her loss to Morgan. She announced Saturday night that she had been cleared and that her ankle is 100 percent. What Matches Are Announced for Raw? Aside from the Vaquer-Lynch matchup, fans will also see Bayley vs. Lyra Valkyria in a No DQ match, Raquel Rodriguez will defend the Women’s Intercontinental Championship against Iyo Sky , while Chad Gable and Dragon Lee face Big Cass and Ethan Page in a tag-team match. Match Stipulation Becky Lynch vs. Stephanie Vaquer Women’s World Championship No. 1 contender’s match Bayley vs. Lyra Valkyria No Disqualification Raquel Rodriguez vs. Iyo Sky Women’s Intercontinental Championship Chad Gable and Dragon Lee vs. Big Cass and Ethan Page Tag team match What Else Could Happen on Raw? I’d also expect to see some developments in the Bloodline-946 drama — even if it is subtle. WWE is also advertising Oba Femi, Penta, Sol Ruca and The Judgment Day for the Fresno show, though no matches have been announced for them. What’s on the Crown Jewel Card So Far? As of now, this is the card in place for Crown Jewel. Match Stipulation Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn Champion vs. Champion for the men’s Crown Jewel Championship Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green Champion vs. Champion for the women’s Crown Jewel Championship Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton Last Man Standing Perhaps we see one or two matches added from this week’s Raw and/or SmackDown. I wouldn’t be surprised to see a cash-in at Crown Jewel. If we only get four matches scheduled, it could be creating time for a cash-in match. The two Champion vs. Champion matches pit all four of WWE’s top singles champions against each other. Crown Jewel streams live from Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, starting at noon ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Yellow line debate divides NASCAR fans after Talladega Cup finish
item.description: Motorsport photo On the final lap of Sunday's NASCAR Cup race at Talladega Superspeedway, Kyle Larson entered Turn 3 in 11th place, but rapidly cut through the pack to snatch victory away from Ricky Stenhouse Jr . and William Byron . However, some people raised questions over the pivotal pass for the win, and if Larson dipped his left-side tires below the yellow line as he ripped by Todd Gilliland in the tri-oval. Chastain came under similar scrutiny. Earlier in the same lap, there was an entirely different moment that brought the rule into question when Austin Hill cut under Kyle Larson for the lead at the exit of Turn 2 and dipped his left-sides under the yellow line. Hill ultimately finished at the tail-end of the lead lap anyway after he lost power coming to the checkered flag. The rule reads: "Section 8.3.2: Vehicles must race above the double yellow lines around the entire race track. If in NASCAR's judgement, the vehicle(s) goes beneath the double yellow lines to improve its position, vehicle(s) will be black-flagged. If in NASCAR's judgement a vehicle forces another vehicle beneath the double yellow lines (in an effort to stop the advancement/pass) the vehicle may be black-flagged." item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo On the final lap of Sunday's NASCAR Cup race at Talladega Superspeedway, Kyle Larson entered Turn 3 in 11th place, but rapidly cut through the pack to snatch victory away from Ricky Stenhouse Jr . and William Byron . However, some people raised questions over the pivotal pass for the win, and if Larson dipped his left-side tires below the yellow line as he ripped by Todd Gilliland in the tri-oval. Chastain came under similar scrutiny. Earlier in the same lap, there was an entirely different moment that brought the rule into question when Austin Hill cut under Kyle Larson for the lead at the exit of Turn 2 and dipped his left-sides under the yellow line. Hill ultimately finished at the tail-end of the lead lap anyway after he lost power coming to the checkered flag. The rule reads: "Section 8.3.2: Vehicles must race above the double yellow lines around the entire race track. If in NASCAR's judgement, the vehicle(s) goes beneath the double yellow lines to improve its position, vehicle(s) will be black-flagged. If in NASCAR's judgement a vehicle forces another vehicle beneath the double yellow lines (in an effort to stop the advancement/pass) the vehicle may be black-flagged." item.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) takes off on a run Sunday, Oct. (Grace Hollars/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images) Some trade rumors keep coming back, and the one linking the Green Bay Packers to Jonathan Taylor just took another lap. ESPN’s Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported Sunday, Oct. 25, that the Packers are a possible landing spot for the Indianapolis Colts’ star running back. “Locked On Packers” host Peter Bukowski chose to connect that report to another Colts name already tied to Green Bay. However, the same report raised the big question of whether Indianapolis is even willing to sell, and a couple of fans weren’t sold on Green Bay buying, either. Peter Bukowski Connects the Dots Between Two Colts Stars The report came in a rundown of the Colts’ deadline options after Indianapolis fired general manager Chris Ballard. It listed the Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos as “among the teams that have, or are expected, to ponder the possibility of a trade for the star running back.” The same report also listed DeForest Buckner among the Colts drawing interest around the league. The 32-year-old defensive tackle is on an expiring contract and set to hit free agency in 2027. Tyler Brooke had already reported that the Packers called on him. This weekend, Super Bowl champion Russell Wilson also tapped the Packers as dark-horse contenders for a trade for Taylor . RUN YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Ultimate GM Simulator Bukowski decided to put the two together a few hours after ESPN’s story dropped. “The Packers have shown interest in Jonathan Taylor before,” he wrote, before delivering his verdict: “It wouldn’t be surprising at all if they’re gauging cost on more than one guy.” Green Bay has kicked these tires before, too. ESPN reported that Green Bay looked into a deal for the former Wisconsin standout back in August 2023, with Indianapolis asking for wide receiver Christian Watson and more. The Colts may not be in a rush to move him now. Sources informed of the team’s thinking told ESPN that owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as “a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild,” and that prying him loose would likely take premium draft pick compensation. Taylor’s 587 rushing yards through Week 7 rank fifth in the NFL, and his eight rushing touchdowns are tied for first. RUN YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Ultimate GM Simulator Bukowski decided to put the two together a few hours after ESPN’s story dropped. “The Packers have shown interest in Jonathan Taylor before,” he wrote, before delivering his verdict: “It wouldn’t be surprising at all if they’re gauging cost on more than one guy.” Green Bay has kicked these tires before, too. ESPN reported that Green Bay looked into a deal for the former Wisconsin standout back in August 2023, with Indianapolis asking for wide receiver Christian Watson and more. The Colts may not be in a rush to move him now. Sources informed of the team’s thinking told ESPN that owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as “a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild,” and that prying him loose would likely take premium draft pick compensation. Taylor’s 587 rushing yards through Week 7 rank fifth in the NFL, and his eight rushing touchdowns are tied for first. The 27-year-old is due $16 million next season and nearly $18 million in 2028 on the $44 million extension he signed just before the season. Trade Proposal Arrives From Fans Alongside Two Arguments for Staying Put One fan skipped the hand-wringing and went straight to haggling: “Lloyd & a 3rd round pick.” Another fan took the opposite tack: “The Packers are not going to trade for a 28-year-old RB when they already have a 28-year-old RB.” That post landed a few hours before Josh Jacobs, who missed the season’s first six games, made his 2026 debut against the Detroit Lions. Another fan decided to argue against a deal on roster grounds, opening with “It’s a fun hypothetical but this would be so reckless for Green Bay.” The same fan went on to argue that “the run game has bigger issues than simply just adding a RB” and that “the focus needs to be on collecting draft capital.” On Sunday, Green Bay ran 19 times for 60 yards in a 20-17 loss that ended on Jake Bates’ 22-yard field goal as time expired. Jacobs carried 11 times for 36 yards and caught a 25-yard touchdown pass, while Lloyd added 20 yards on six carries. CHECK THE DEPTH CHARTS: PFN’s NFL Depth Charts The Packers, now 4-3 and fourth in the NFC North, host the Carolina Panthers on Thursday, Oct. 29. According to ESPN, sources informed of the Colts’ thinking believed the plan was to try to win at Minnesota, at the Jacksonville Jaguars, and against the Dallas Cowboys before the Nov. 10 deadline. The first of those games ended in a 16-10 loss to the Vikings that dropped them to 2-5. The same report said that if that stretch doesn’t go their way, new chief of personnel Ed Dodds will work with Irsay-Gordon and the rest of the Colts brass to trade away assets and build toward the future. Indianapolis visits Jacksonville on Nov. 1 and hosts Dallas on Nov. 8, with just two Sundays left before the deadline arrives. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Tyrese Haliburton quickly walks back Dr. J comment about self-lob dunk
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Tyrese Haliburton quickly walks back Dr. J comment about self-lob dunk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indiana Pacers have plenty of reason for optimism this season as star point guard Tyrese Haliburton has made his return after being sidelined for all of last season due to injury. The Pacers are 2-1 to start the season , with a recent win against the Brooklyn Nets, and Haliburton stole the show with a lob to himself via bounce pass while on a break. It just so happened that the Pacers were playing in retro ABA jerseys, and for Tyrese Haliburton, those jerseys were the reason why he decided to attempt the lob dunk off his own pass. “Sometimes you just got to commit to the bit, you know what I’m saying. I didn’t really think I was gonna do it,” Haliburton quipped. “You can’t think about it cause otherwise you’ll mess it up. So I just committed fully. I think it was the ABA jerseys, I felt like Dr. J or something.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In true hilarious Haliburton fashion, he jokingly walked back his comments and told the reporter not to quote him on saying he felt like the great Julius Irving. Including that lob dunk, Haliburton finished the game with a game-high 24 points in 31 minutes. He also added four rebounds, 10 assists, and two steals. He shot 8-of-13 from the field, 4-of-7 from the 3-point line and 4-of-5 from the free-throw line. Through the Pacers’ first two games of the season, Haliburton is averaging 20.5 points, 4.0 rebounds, 9.5 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 blocked shots with splits of 50 percent shooting from the field, 20 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 100 percent shooting from the free-throw line. Related: Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton sends immediate message after Jalen Williams injury Related: Caitlin Clark catches Pacers’ home opener vs. Mavs

item.title: San Diego Wave keep NWSL Shield hopes alive with draw against Boston
item.description: San Diego Wave FC midfielder Gia Corley (11) celebrates her goal with teammate Melanie Barcenas (7) during an NWSL soccer game against Boston Legacy, Sunday, October 25, 2026 in San Diego, California. SAN DIEGO — Boston Legacy FC snapped San Diego Wave FC’s five-game winning streak with a stunning 73rd-minute equalizer, resulting in a 2-2 draw at Snapdragon Stadium. The Wave remain in contention for the NWSL Shield heading into Decision Day. San Diego (17-4-8, 55 points) must defeat Bay FC next Sunday, Nov. 1, while Gotham FC (17-7-5, 58 points) must lose to the Utah Royals to finish tied on points. The tiebreaker would then be goal differential. After a scoreless first half, Boston’s Annie Karich opened the scoring in the 48th minute. San Diego responded with two goals in three minutes: Gia Corley equalized before an own goal by Laís Araújo gave the Wave a 2-1 lead. Alba Caño then leveled the match with a rocket from outside the box. Boston, which has struggled in its inaugural season, entered Sunday’s match with no playoff hopes after being eliminated from contention last month. The Legacy were looking to build momentum heading into next season after winning their previous two matches. Meanwhile, the second-place Wave were pursuing their second NWSL Shield in five seasons. Wave rookie midfielder Lia Godfrey scored in the 35th minute, but her goal was disallowed after a VAR review determined she was narrowly offside, keeping the match scoreless. San Diego Wave FC midfielder Lia Godfrey fights for the ball against Boston Legacy midfielder Bárbara Olivieri during an NWSL soccer game, Sunday, October 25, 2026 in San Diego, California. Miguel Mota - The Sporting Tribune San Diego Wave FC midfielder Lia Godfrey fights for the ball against Boston Legacy midfielder Bárbara Olivieri during an NWSL soccer game, Sunday, October 25, 2026 in San Diego, California. Jonas Eidevall’s squad controlled much of the opening 45 minutes, holding 61% possession and recording two more shots than the Legacy at halftime. Boston’s defense held firm, but the Legacy capitalized on an opportunity three minutes into the second half. After a short corner, Sarah Schupansky sent a cross into a crowded penalty area that deflected off Sandra Paños’ glove. Karich was positioned near the left post and finished from point-blank range to give Boston the lead. It was her first goal of the season. It didn’t take long for San Diego to respond. On a fast break, Wave forward Melanie Barcenas carried the ball into the attacking third before finding Corley as she entered the left side of the box. Corley took one touch before sending a low shot underneath a defender and past a diving goalkeeper. The ball struck the bottom-right post and went in, tying the match in the 51st minute. It was Corley’s fourth goal of the season and her fifth goal contribution in the past six matches. The attacking midfielder has continued to deliver for San Diego during its late-season push. Barcenas now has nine

item.title: Puka Nacua addresses reinjury fears after MRI reveals calf injury details
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Puka Nacua has provided an update on his calf injury after helping the Los Angeles Rams secure a 35-21 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. The wide receiver entered the game as questionable after picking up the injury during practice. However, an MRI reportedly revealed nothing significant, allowing him to take the field. Nacua finished with eight receptions for 68 yards and a touchdown as the Rams ended their two-game losing streak. Puka Nacua explains how he is managing his calf injury Speaking to reporters, Nacua explained how the injury happened and addressed concerns about suffering a recurrence. “Just trying to run, and deceleration after, guys, it kind of tapped off on the play. I just planted, and just felt something in my lower calf,” he said. The Rams star also confirmed that the MRI had not revealed anything significant, although he was unsure which specific muscle had been affected. Nacua admitted that avoiding the fear of reinjury was part of his preparation before facing the Raiders. “I try to mentally prepare and say that I’m full focus and being able to play in the game and kind of letting some of those worries and fears go,” he explained. The calf problem comes after Nacua missed two games earlier in the season with a groin injury. He also dealt with a hip issue during training camp and the pre-season. Despite those setbacks, the receiver remains focused on making himself available for Los Angeles. “Just trying to figure out how I can best feel out there on Sunday and doing everything I can,” Nacua said. He also praised the Rams’ training staff for helping him return to action, while highlighting his communication with quarterback Matthew Stafford as an important part of staying prepared despite missing practice repetitions. The Rams now face the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals before their bye week. Nacua’s involvement in practice will be worth monitoring as the team looks to manage his workload and keep him available for the coming games. His performance against Las Vegas showed that he can still make an impact, but the Rams will need to balance that production with the importance of protecting his long-term fitness. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander keeps faith in Thunder despite Jalen Williams injury
item.description: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images Shai Gilgeous-Alexander keeps faith in Thunder despite Jalen Williams injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . OKLAHOMA CITY — Oklahoma City Thunder All-Star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander ’s eyes filled up with tears talking about Jalen Williams’ leg injury at the end of a 108-101 win against the LA Clippers. As the Thunder were putting the finishing touches on their third victory of the young regular season, Williams suffered a gruesome left ankle injury . He was carted off the court in a stretcher before giving fans in Oklahoma City two thumbs up. Gilgeous-Alexander, who was emotional during his walk-off interview, composed himself before speaking to reporters on how the Thunder plan to move forward after losing Williams in a devastating fashion. “It sucks but it’s part of the game. We have a team for a reason. We got guys that are ready to step in place and make a difference out there on the floor,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “Hold the fort down until those guys come back and also support those guys in their journey. Super unfortunate. All three of them, I guess, tonight. But yeah, we’ll be OK.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It sucks but it’s part of the game. We have a team for a reason. item.title: Chiefs’ Travis Kelce reaches huge career milestone on National Tight Ends Day
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Chiefs’ Travis Kelce reaches huge career milestone on National Tight Ends Day appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Travis Kelce was a limited participant during practice ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs’ Sunday night showdown against the Seattle Seahawks . But the Chiefs tight end always looked on course to play on National Tight Ends Day. Not only did Kelce play, but he also made history against the Seahawks. Kelce climbed up to No. 5 on the list of most receptions in NFL history . He overtook Indianapolis Colts legend Marvin Harrison with 1,103 catches. As NFL Network and ESPN reporter Mike Garafolo pointed out on X, formerly Twitter, tight ends now make up three of the top five spots in the all-time receptions list. Tony Gonzalez and Jason Witten are the other two joining Kelce behind receivers Jerry Rice and Larry Fitzgerald. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) At age 37, Travis Kelce is proving to everyone that he is not yet completely washed . He may not be putting up the brilliant numbers like he did during his prime, but he is still a key contributor on the Chiefs. Heading into the game against the Seahawks, he had 20 catches for 299 yards and two touchdowns. He is second on the team behind Xavier Worthy in receptions, first by a wide margin in receiving yards, and tied for first in receiving touchdowns. That’s not bad for an aging tight end who has contemplated retirement for the last few seasons. It’s also a bit of an indictment on the Chiefs that they continue to lean so heavily on a 37-year-old Kelce in the receiving game. That’s not ideal, especially if they hope to compete for a Super Bowl again. Still, what Travis Kelce is doing is nothing short of amazing, and he deserves to be celebrated for his latest career milestone. Related: Did Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker III dodge ex-Seahawks teammates after SNF loss Related: Chiefs pick off Sam Darnold just before SNF halftime

item.title: Nashville's Shield standard, El Tráfico fireworks & more from Matchday 32
item.description: Nashville's Shield standard, El Tráfico fireworks & more from Matchday 32 By Charles Boehm Finally, we’ve reached the final sprint. With the 2026 US Open Cup and Canadian Championship tournaments in the books (congrats St. Louis CITY SC and Forge FC) and a range of rescheduled matches played, it’s all about the league. One more busy Wednesday night, a wall-to-wall Halloween weekend of action and then Decision Day on Nov. 7. That, plus a FIFA international window, is all that remains before the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs spark into life. Nine teams from each conference will take part. Four have clinched their spot in the East; five have done so in the West. Even now, only one team in each, CF Montréal and Sporting Kansas City , have been officially eliminated. So much can happen in the next couple of weeks, let alone in the postseason. It’s the most wonderful time of the MLS year, and you could taste it across Matchday 32. Nashville SC To the ‘Yotes goes the Shield Congratulations to Nashville SC , who clinched the 2026 Supporters’ Shield with a sunny 2-0 weekend-opening win at Montréal that felt inevitable, both on the day and in the calendar, given how dominant, how far ahead of the field B.J. Callaghan’s Coyotes have been for months. A CFMTL side rotated and reeling from midweek heartbreak in the Canadian Championship final were straightforward prey for Sam Surridge , Hany Mukhtar and the rest of an NSC unit who have locked down home-field advantage for the duration of the playoffs, tied the record for fastest march to the Shield and can still break 2024 Inter Miami 's MLS record for most points in a season (74) by taking five from the nine in play across their final three regular-season games. The best way I can explain them is to quote a few bars from my colleague Ben Wright, who’s set the standard with his NSC coverage both here and on SixOneFive Soccer : “Nashville have been dominant in MLS this season. They've racked up 21 wins so far, four more than the closest team. They've lost just three games, three fewer than the next team. They've outscored their opponents by 43 goals this year, and haven't dropped out of first place in the table since May. With three games left to play, they're just five points away from setting the all-time points record.” These ‘Yotes are one of the most complete teams this league have ever seen, and they aim to prove it by hoisting more hardware in a few weeks. “I think for one, two weeks we can be European, celebrate the championship,” joked Mukhtar. “But then we have to get back to how the system is here, the playoffs and all that. We need to be ready. We know that it's a new season in the playoffs, and we will make sure that we are all ready.” WATCH: Mukhtar, Surridge lead Nashville to Supporters’ Shield LA Galaxy El Tráfico delivers, as usual What more can we say about the Los Angeles derby? item.content:encoded: Nashville's Shield standard, El Tráfico fireworks & more from Matchday 32 By Charles Boehm Finally, we’ve reached the final sprint. With the 2026 US Open Cup and Canadian Championship tournaments in the books (congrats St. Louis CITY SC and Forge FC) and a range of rescheduled matches played, it’s all about the league. One more busy Wednesday night, a wall-to-wall Halloween weekend of action and then Decision Day on Nov. 7. That, plus a FIFA international window, is all that remains before the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs spark into life. Nine teams from each conference will take part. Four have clinched their spot in the East; five have done so in the West. Even now, only one team in each, CF Montréal and Sporting Kansas City , have been officially eliminated. So much can happen in the next couple of weeks, let alone in the postseason. It’s the most wonderful time of the MLS year, and you could taste it across Matchday 32. Nashville SC To the ‘Yotes goes the Shield Congratulations to Nashville SC , who clinched the 2026 Supporters’ Shield with a sunny 2-0 weekend-opening win at Montréal that felt inevitable, both on the day and in the calendar, given how dominant, how far ahead of the field B.J. Callaghan’s Coyotes have been for months. A CFMTL side rotated and reeling from midweek heartbreak in the Canadian Championship final were straightforward prey for Sam Surridge , Hany Mukhtar and the rest of an NSC unit who have locked down home-field advantage for the duration of the playoffs, tied the record for fastest march to the Shield and can still break 2024 Inter Miami 's MLS record for most points in a season (74) by taking five from the nine in play across their final three regular-season games. The best way I can explain them is to quote a few bars from my colleague Ben Wright, who’s set the standard with his NSC coverage both here and on SixOneFive Soccer : “Nashville have been dominant in MLS this season. They've racked up 21 wins so far, four more than the closest team. They've lost just three games, three fewer than the next team. They've outscored their opponents by 43 goals this year, and haven't dropped out of first place in the table since May. With three games left to play, they're just five points away from setting the all-time points record.” These ‘Yotes are one of the most complete teams this league have ever seen, and they aim to prove it by hoisting more hardware in a few weeks. “I think for one, two weeks we can be European, celebrate the championship,” joked Mukhtar. “But then we have to get back to how the system is here, the playoffs and all that. We need to be ready. We know that it's a new season in the playoffs, and we will make sure that we are all ready.” WATCH: Mukhtar, Surridge lead Nashville to Supporters’ Shield LA Galaxy El Tráfico delivers, as usual What more can we say about the Los Angeles derby? Wherever the teams are in the standings, whatever’s going on in their respective worlds, LAFC vs. LA Galaxy almost always entertains, and the SoCal rivals closed out the weekend with another superb spectacle at BMO Stadium on Sunday Night Soccer presented by Continental Tire. After 98 minutes of punch-and-counterpunch, hammer-and-tongs, blood-and-guts soccer that pulsated right down to the last kick of the game, the Galaxy escaped with a 2-2 tie thanks to a clutch brace from Joseph Paintsil , who might not even have been in the starting lineup had a late-breaking illness not prevented Marco Reus from taking part. It’s been a tough year for the Ghanaian winger overall. But when LA accelerate into space and get him out on the run, he remains a true game-breaker – and shouts out to the underrated Robert Taylor , who made a key series of plays to break this game open: While LAFC will bitterly rue the two goals they saw disallowed for offside, they showed real guts to rally for a draw and pushed desperately ‘til the end. Hopefully, interim coach Xavi Tamarit saw what the rest of us did when he finally shifted Denis Bouanga back out to his usual spot on the left flank late, and just lets him cook out there from now on. Red Bull New York RBNY kids seize the spotlight Speaking of ace match coverage… how about this lede on Red Bull New York ’s surprise 2-0 win over Inter Miami from The Sporting News’ Kyle Bonn ? "Fans flocked to Sports Illustrated Stadium on Saturday evening to be wowed by Lionel Messi. Instead, they were treated to the Adri Mehmeti show." That’s how good RBNY’s 17-year-old midfield tempo-setter was in the acquisition of these massive three points for their playoff hunt, keeping their noses above the red line for at least a few more days. Head coach Michael Bradley had promised that his young side would stand tall against their vaunted visitors, and so they did. “The maturity he has is unbelievable,” said Mehmeti’s midfield mate and fellow wunderkind Mohammed Sofo . “The vision he has, he knows when to play forward, when to calm down. Sometimes he does things [where] I'm like, 'wow.' For me, as a No. 8 or also as a No. 10, I try to find myself in the pockets, and sometimes he finds me with just two touches. Other players need to take a first touch, look for it, and then play it. But for him... second touch, he finds you.” Conversely, Miami flashed some real red flags in this one, with Messi among the substitutes to manage his minutes after flying to Spain and back to receive the prestigious Princess of Asturias Award for Sports. Still, resting the GOAT will probably prove the right move: Even with New England pulling level with IMCF on points and well ahead on the wins tiebreaker in second place in the Eastern Conference How will the West be won? St. Louis CITY SC While Nashville have clinched the Shield and the East, the West is far from won, thanks to losses by first- and second-placed sides Vancouver and St. Louis on their respective trips to Rocky Mountain altitude. We’re inclined to give CITY SC some leeway for their 3-0 thumping at the hands of Real Salt Lake given their emotional triumph , via 120 minutes and a penalty-kick shootout, in Wednesday’s US Open Cup final in Columbus, which prompted Sigi Schmid MLS Coach of the Year contender Yoann Damet to rejigger his starting XI. Tomáš Ostrák ’s silly second yellow card just before halftime threw the Ravioli Boyz behind the 8-ball, and RSL rookie sensation Sergi Solans earned man of the match via a brace of back-post tap-ins. But the highlight-reel play was this long-distance banger from Dominik Marczuk , who saw a left-footed piledriver saved by Ben Lundt and simply uncorked another one with his right a few seconds later: Vancouver Whitecaps FC We reckon the wobbling Whitecaps have more to worry about after a 1-0 loss to a Colorado outfit who’d been riding a five-game winless skid. The Rapids dominated the run of play here and drew seven saves out of goalkeeper Yohei Takaoka , only to finally break through on a quirky sequence in which a parried ball softly doinked off the top of the crossbar to present Morgan Whittaker with the pointest of point-blank finishes. The ‘Caps clearly miss Thomas Müller ; they’ve won just one of the four matches he’s missed with a hamstring injury. Head coach Jesper Sørensen says the German legend “should be able to be playing soon,” and it’s sensible to structure Müller’s timeline around the playoffs, where VWFC will likely keep hold of home-field advantage in Round One. Yet much of that daunting aura they accrued during their splendid 2025 has ebbed away since the summer departure of midfield motor Sebastian Berhalter. FC Dallas Moosepowered in Dallas The West frontrunners’ stumbles opened the door for their nearest pursuers FC Dallas and the San Jose Earthquakes , who just happened to be facing off at Toyota Stadium Saturday night. It took 83 minutes to break the deadlock, yet that would cue an opening of the proverbial floodgates. And the name of that flood, as usual for FCD, was Petar Musa . After

item.title: What Browns’ Todd Monken said about Deshaun Watson pulling another rabbit out of hat
item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images What Browns’ Todd Monken said about Deshaun Watson pulling another rabbit out of hat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Todd Monken didn’t mince words about Deshaun Watson ’s clutch efforts following his game-winning drive in the Cleveland Browns’ 27-24 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday afternoon. Watson has been playing in the NFL since 2017, going through his fifth season with the Browns. Following off-field controversies and injuries, the 2026 season marks his healthiest season in years. Watson is off to a strong start for Cleveland, helping them exceed expectations with one of the best records in the AFC. They earned another win after beating Tennessee, seeing the start of Monken’s head coaching career be incredible. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Monken reflected on the win after the game, per reporter Mary Kay Cabot. He noted how Watson’s lone interception wasn’t his fault as he expressed how impactful the quarterback can be in clutch moments. “The turnover on the slant where Denzel got shut off — he’s got to cross face and quarterback has got to be able to trust that,” Monken said. “(Deshaun) has something in him to make plays when it counts. We’re trying to flat line our play earlier in the game to be more consistent.” #Browns Todd Monken on Deshaun Watson’s 5th 4th-quarter game-winning drive of the season for a 27-24 victory over the #Titans pic.twitter.com/xdHbNrPyGk — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) October 25, 2026 How Deshaun Watson, Browns played against Titans Deshaun Watson and the Browns continue their strong start to the season after beating the Titans. Todd Monken hopes the winning can continue as they make a dark horse case for a playoff spot. Both teams traded blows throughout the course of regulation, seeing Cleveland only lead 17-14 at halftime. Tennessee tried fighting back as they notched things at 17 apiece, but the Browns responded with 10 crucial points to escape with the road win. Watson completed 25 out of 36 passes for 308 yards and an interception while rushing three times for 19 yards and a touchdown. Quinshon Judkins rushed 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns, while KC Concepcion commanded the receiving corps with eight catches for 129 yards. The Browns will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8 as kickoff commences on Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET. Related: Browns’ Todd Monken points out concerning trend after beating Titans Related: Browns’ Deshaun Watson opens up on ‘teaching moment’ for Denzel Boston in Titans game

item.title: Fred Warner Doesn’t Hold Back After 49ers’ Loss to Falcons
item.description: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers suffered their first loss of the 2026 NFL season, losing 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 on Oct. 25 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. San Francisco couldn’t overcome the turnovers that they committed during the game, as the Niners had two interceptions from Brock Purdy and two fumbles lost. Moreover, Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. went 25-for-34 on his pass attempts for 213 passing yards and three touchdowns against the 49ers’ defense. After the loss to Atlanta, Niners linebacker Fred Warner, who recorded 13 tackles in the defeat, spoke to the media and didn’t hold back his thoughts regarding what went wrong for the team. “We just didn’t play complementary football in all three phases,” Warner told reporters postgame . “Defensively, I felt like it was super sloppy all day. Of course, I have to look at myself and the way I’m communicating with the rest of the group and the way we’re executing. “But at the end of the day, you can’t beat yourself. They came out, they played better than us, and we have to deal with that result… Unfortunately, we’re not going undefeated this year. That’s how I look at it. I said all along, it’s not just about winning. We have to continue to get better as a team. I feel like today we didn’t get better. We took a step back.” Fred Warner Wants 49ers to Make the Most Out of Bye Week While Warner’s comments were on the negative side as the Niners head into their bye week, the team can use this time to address issues that could pop up again later in the season. “That doesn’t mean that we can’t use this bye the right way, get healthy, get our mind right for what we have ahead of us, and be better going forward,” Warner added . “I’m excited about the challenge. I love that group in there. This is the most fun I’ve had playing football, playing with this group. “We have so much talent. We have so many guys that play the right way. If we can clean things up, which I know we will, then we have a great chance every single week that we step out there.” San Francisco’s undefeated start wasn’t the main goal, as the team aspires to be the last team standing with the Lombardi Trophy. The loss against the Falcons showed that the 49ers aren’t a juggernaut, and if they aren’t on their game, the Niners can be beat. George Kittle on Niners’ Loss to Falcons in Week 7 Meanwhile, George Kittle was also blunt about how the 49ers performed against Atlanta, as this isn’t the way the team wanted to head into the bye week, as they now have to sit on this loss for a couple of weeks. “I would have much rather won, but the great thing about losing is never great,” Kittle told reporters postgame . “When you do lose, especially in this organization, it makes everybody really look at themselves in the mirror. All I think it’s going to do is spark an even bigger fire underneath us. All we want to do is win. We want to continue to win. “We want to put good tape out there. Sometimes, I think

item.title: Who plays on 'Monday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 7 game
item.description: Who plays on 'Monday Night Football' tonight? Time, TV channel, schedule, live stream for NFL Week 7 game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Does anyone want to win the NFC East? "Monday Night Football" might provide the answer. While two NFC East teams facing off doesn't necessarily guarantee one will win -- just ask the Giants and Commanders -- the odds are that someone will emerge from Monday's primetime showdown well-positioned in a weak division. The other will spiral to 2-5. The Eagles enter "Monday Night Football" on a four-game losing streak with a number of injuries, including the season-long absence of Jalen Hurts after he was diagnosed with blood clots in his lungs, but Philadelphia is getting RB Saquon Barkley back in the mix. For the Cowboys , it's more about getting right than getting healthy. Dallas might have to win in spite of its defense this season, but Brian Schottenheimer's offense knows it has to be better than it was against the Packers in Week 6 for the Cowboys to reach their goals. With that, here's what you need to know to watch "Monday Night Football" in Week 7. Who plays on Monday Night Football tonight? A 2-0 start to the season won’t stop the chatter on possible roster upgrades in the long run and in the playoffs. One suggested proposal by a fan is a move for Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis, with Jarred Vanderbilt being the trade chip. According to Lakers Insider Jovan Buha, any potential trade for Porzingis is not impossible, but the chances are slim. “This is an interesting one because first and foremost, we don’t know if Kristaps Porzingis is ever going to play in the NBA again,” Buha said . “There is the recent reports from ESPN and Shams Charania about him being contemplating retirement based on all the medical stuff he is dealing with right now. “But he does have a $20 million contract for this year and a player option for next year.
