(Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) Getty A lot can still happen around the league before the trade deadline, especially with the Los Angeles Lakers. A 2-0 start to the season won’t stop the chatter on possible roster upgrades in the long run and in the playoffs. One suggested proposal by a fan is a move for Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis, with Jarred Vanderbilt being the trade chip. According to Lakers Insider Jovan Buha, any potential trade for Porzingis is not impossible, but the chances are slim. “This is an interesting one because first and foremost, we don’t know if Kristaps Porzingis is ever going to play in the NBA again,” Buha said . “There is the recent reports from ESPN and Shams Charania about him being contemplating retirement based on all the medical stuff he is dealing with right now. “But he does have a $20 million contract for this year and a player option for next year. I assume unless he retires, he will pick up that player option.” Porzingis will always be a wildcard move any day. His health history is alarming, but he is a championship-caliber big who could be an elite backup option to Walker Kessler . Lakers Insider Shares Thoughts on Possible Trade for Kristaps Porzingis Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) Porzingis joined Golden State at the last trade deadline, and it hasn’t been the most favorable of stints, considering what they gave up to acquire him. It hasn’t been that the 31-year-old former All-Star center hasn’t lived up to expectations on the floor, but he hasn’t been readily available. He played only 15 games for the Warriors. That alone is every red flag that the Lakers need but the idea is that Porzingis will not be a starter. However, according to Buha, the financial aspect is another hindrance as the trade may not be feasible for the Lakers. “There is a massive risk here, if you do this trade… you take on some additional money and I wonder if Golden State will throw something in,” Buha added. “But to this point, when we are talking about Vando over the summer, what I propose when people throw out the Vando trade. Realistically the only way I see L.A. trading Vando is if they trade him for another sub-par contract. Another contract that a team is trying to get off from.” Vanderbilt has been one of the top names on the Lakers trade list this summer but he is still in L.A. However, he is yet to feature in the first couple of games which indicates that he has fallen off the rotation. But Buha suggests that any trade for him won’t be for a higher salary earner. Weighing Whether L.A. Needs Porzingis The Lakers’ only like-for-like backup option for Kessler is Kevon Looney and there have been some eyebrows raised over leaning on the veteran if their starting center is absent. Kessler has started the season strong with 26 and 22 points respectively in his first two games. The Lakers are getting their full money’s worth but they will keep in the back of their minds that he may not always be available. A reliable backuo option to the 7-foot-2 center has been speculated with Porzingis joining the queue. A move for Porzingis could be a chance for the Lakers to free up some deeper rotational players but even at that, their cap space will be tight. “If you do take on Porzingis you are still under the first apron, you are going to be close there,” Buha said. “You could throw in (Jaden) Hardy, you could throw in Bronny (James)… You could throw in Looney, maybe go back to Golden State.” Porzingis will be an ideal backup to Kessler if he manages to stay on the floor. In those handful of games for the Warriors, he averaged 16.1 points and 5.3 rebounds as well as 1.1 blocks per game. But the tax has always been whether he can stay on the floot for a sustained period. item.title: Lions’ Brian Branch reacts to massive INT in injury return
item.description: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Lions’ Brian Branch reacts to massive INT in injury return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions earned a big win over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. It was a close game that could have gone either way. But the Detroit defense stood tall, having received a big boost with Brian Branch ’s return from injury. Branch played his first game since December 2025 on Sunday. He had some rust, but overall, he did what the team needed him to do. In the fourth quarter, he even picked off a pass from Jordan Love. The Lions shared his reaction to the play after the game. So glad you're back, BB! pic.twitter.com/ilm5XUBKrc Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Detroit Lions (@Lions) October 26, 2026 The Lions offense didn’t capitalize on the interception and allowed Green Bay to tie the game. Detroit nearly handed the Packers the lead as well. They failed to convert a fourth down from their own 24-yard line late in the contest. However, Detroit’s defense stood tall again, forcing the Packers to kick another field goal. This time, Trey Smack missed the kick, hooking it to the right. This gave the Lions a chance to march down the field and win this game. The Lions did just that. Detroit’s offense did not give the ball back. They went down and kicked a field goal with no time remaining to clinch a crucial 20-17 win over their NFC North rivals. The Packers are now 4-3 and sit last in the division after this loss. Detroit is now 4-2 on the season and remains undefeated at home. Next week, they will look to remain undefeated at Ford Field. The Lions play host to the undefeated Minnesota Vikings on November 1. Related: Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs reveals NSFW reaction to Dan Campbell’s decision vs. Packers Related: Lions spammed all the emotes after crucial penalty in Packers win

item.title: Several OKC Thunder players react to Jalen Williams' injury in win over Clippers
item.description: In a postgame setting that felt like a funeral, the Oklahoma City Thunder were all out of sorts. Usually, when talking to the local media, they're detailed with their words and extremely calculated. But for obvious reasons, things were different after their 108-101 win over the LA Clippers . Jalen Williams' gruesome-looking injury had everybody in the Paycom Center shell-shocked. From Thunder players to the OKC crowd to arena workers. With 1:14 to go in regulation, Kris Dunn collided with him mid-air on a drive to the rim. He landed badly on his left leg. It looked like it snapped in the wrong direction. The Thunder medical staff had to cover Williams' leg with towels. He was eventually stretchered off the floor. Shai Gilgeous-Alexande wept tears; Chet Holmgren knelt in prayer; and Alex Caruso looked the other way in total disbelief. Here's everything the Thunder said about Williams' injury — as it looks like it'll be a season-defining one for the worse: Mark Daigneault "Yeah, those are tough, man. I don't know. We're not doing great. That's tough on the guys. Everyone empathizes. I think both teams in those situations. Not doing great." Shai Gilgeous-Alexander "You've got to play the hand you're dealt in life. It is what it is. It sucks, but it's part of the game. But we have a team for a reason. We have a guy who can step in place. Make a difference out there on the floor. Hold the fort down until those guys come back. But also support those guys in their journey." "He just loves playing, loves the competition. That's who he is. I have no doubt in my mind he'll be back. He'll be better than he was before. Just like how he handled the last couple of injuries. It's unfortunate. His luck so far. He's up for it. He's a warrior." Alex Caruso "There's no getting around feeling bad for Dub, feeling sorry for him. All the emotions that come with somebody getting stretched off the court. That's your teammate. That's been through all the things that he's been through and the adversity he's been through to work and get back and then have something else kind of freak happen to. It stings." This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Several OKC Thunder players react to Jalen Williams' injury in win over Clippers

item.title: Red Wings ‘Calling Around’ To Talk Trade, Friedman Says
item.description: Shawn Horcoff Red Wings Getty The Detroit Red Wings are picking up the horn to see what’s available out there. That’s what insider Elliotte Friedman revealed during the pre-game broadcast leading up to the Heritage Classic on Sunday evening. The notable insider told Jackie Redmond that the GM Shawn Horcoff is calling around the league, but it’s unclear whether the calls involve Dylan Larkin or Simon Edvinsson. “Detroit is calling around now, and I don’t know if it’s for Larkin or it’s for Simon Edvinsson. But they are asking teams about young centers. And we’re not only talking about guys who are in the NHL now, but guys who are also top prospects in organizations.” The comments suggest that the Red Wings aren’t budging from their desire for young talent down the middle. The biggest difference now seems to be that the Red Wings are willing to look at prospects instead of NHL-ready players. That situation could be the key factor that makes a deal happen now, rather than dragging the saga out much longer on either player. Friedman concluded his thoughts by doubling down on Detroit’s expectations at this point. “If there is a good center out there, and even available or not, Detroit is asking about them, if it’s a team Larkin is willing to go to.” Friend of the program @FriedgeHNIC had some scoops for @Jackie_Redmond … Larkin updates, Hellebuyck fallout, the Nikishin contract and more 👀 pic.twitter.com/pPBnDNWvKp — NHLonTNT (@NHL_On_TNT) October 25, 2026 The crucial factor to this point has to be the fact that Horcoff is talking to teams that Larkin has on his trade list. And if there’s a guy out there that moves the needle, it could lead talks to really moving downfield. Red Wings Not Likely Talking to Montreal One of the major issues regarding the Larkin situation specifically is the possibility of a deal with the Montreal Canadiens. While Friedman didn’t seem convinced a deal could happen between the Red Wings and Habs, there might be a bit more to it than that. Canadiens’ insider Marco D’Amico recently tweeted that Red Wings assistant GM Kris Draper had been spotted during a Canadiens game. D’Amico noted it was the second game in a row that Draper had been spotted watching Montreal. Second straight game for Draper watching the Canadiens. https://t.co/w0VAWtSO3L — Marco D'Amico (@mndamico) October 24, 2026 And so, even if the Canadiens are not on Larkin’s trade list, there seems to be at least some interest in seeing what the Habs have to offer. And considering that it’s a center that the Wings are after, one has to think that’s what Draper is following up on. Nothing Happening for Now All told, there is no indication that anything is happening at the moment. The Red Wings are doing their best to see what’s out there. But the fact of the matter is that there is nothing imminent looming on the horizon. Of course, there’s always the possibility that someone steps up much the same way the Devils did in the Connor Hellebuyck situation. That’s why the

item.title: OPENING ODDS: Notre Dame is a massive favorite (again) over the Navy Midshipmen
item.description: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 08: Ty Washington #7 of the Notre Dame Fighting Irish celebrates a touchdown against the Navy Midshipmen at Notre Dame Stadium on November 08, 2025 in South Bend, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Notre Dame Fighting Irish are looking to get up off the mat after their loss to BYU. The Irish had the bye week to try and fix the things that ultimately led to that loss, and now it’s ALL eyes on the Miami game on November 7th as the “make or break” game for Notre Dame. If the Irish can beat the Canes — it basically nullifies the BYU game, but if not… it’s probably going to be another frustrating offseason. Before any of tht can happen, however, Notre Dame has to travel to Foxborough to play the Navy Midshipmen. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, Notre Dame is currently a 30.5 point favorite against the Middies with an over/under of 54.5 points. No one anywhere is going to give the Irish any credit of they cover the spread here — or even if they win 52-0 for that matter. It is what it is, but it may not be as easy as that, and it certainly doesn’t help the Irish get ready for Miami. I don’t know you guys… I kind of feel like this game might be pointless to schedule every year.

item.title: Overreactions, grades for UC Bearcats upset of No. 8 Texas Tech
item.description: The 100th Homecoming football game at the University of Cincinnati was one of the more memorable wins in Bearcats history. UC took the lead midway through the second quarter on a four-yard touchdown pass to Cole Tabb to go up 10-6. They would never trail from that point and Tabb finished with a "dagger" run late in the fourth quarter to give UC a 37-18 lead. The Red Raiders added a touchdown with 59 seconds left, but not long after, UC fans were on the field in a sea of red celebrating a 37-24 triumph over No. 8 Texas Tech. "To beat a No. 8 Texas Tech team with a ton of resources, yeah, this is probably one of the greatest wins I've been a part of," UC head coach Scott Satterfield said. "It's not about the offseason stuff. It's about the overall things that have happened in college football and for our guys to go out there and perform like we did." It's UC's first Top 10 win since beating Notre Dame in South Bend in 2021 and first at home since knocking off No. 7 Rutgers back in 2006. Grading Cincinnati Enquirer's predictions for Cincinnati Bearcats , Texas Tech We predicted a UC Bearcats home loss Outcome: To the delight of the sellout crowd at Nippert Stadium, that was incorrect. Most outlets missed on the game with Texas Tech being a double-digit favorite. The Red Raiders went to the airport with a 13-point defeat. We said UC would need creative ways to gain yards Outcome: Texas Tech was allowing only 82 yards per game rushing and gave Arizona State just 35 rushing yards Oct. 17. After a sluggish first quarter where they had minus-6 yards on the ground, the Bearcats got it in gear and put 21 on the board for a 24-6 halftime lead. They wound up with 252 yards on the ground, 21 yards above their average and quarterback JC French was able to throw for a career-best four touchdowns. We said JC French IV would make plays, but throw his first interception Outcome: His first interception was a pick-six by Peyton Morgan. Brice Pollock broke up a pass intended for Isaiah Johnson. There was originally a targeting call, which would have wiped away the touchdown, but it was reversed on review. On the next series, Amier Boyd picked off French. item.content:encoded: The 100th Homecoming football game at the University of Cincinnati was one of the more memorable wins in Bearcats history. UC took the lead midway through the second quarter on a four-yard touchdown pass to Cole Tabb to go up 10-6. They would never trail from that point and Tabb finished with a "dagger" run late in the fourth quarter to give UC a 37-18 lead. The Red Raiders added a touchdown with 59 seconds left, but not long after, UC fans were on the field in a sea of red celebrating a 37-24 triumph over No. 8 Texas Tech. "To beat a No. 8 Texas Tech team with a ton of resources, yeah, this is probably one of the greatest wins I've been a part of," UC head coach Scott Satterfield said. "It's not about the offseason stuff. It's about the overall things that have happened in college football and for our guys to go out there and perform like we did." It's UC's first Top 10 win since beating Notre Dame in South Bend in 2021 and first at home since knocking off No. 7 Rutgers back in 2006. Grading Cincinnati Enquirer's predictions for Cincinnati Bearcats , Texas Tech We predicted a UC Bearcats home loss Outcome: To the delight of the sellout crowd at Nippert Stadium, that was incorrect. Most outlets missed on the game with Texas Tech being a double-digit favorite. The Red Raiders went to the airport with a 13-point defeat. We said UC would need creative ways to gain yards Outcome: Texas Tech was allowing only 82 yards per game rushing and gave Arizona State just 35 rushing yards Oct. 17. After a sluggish first quarter where they had minus-6 yards on the ground, the Bearcats got it in gear and put 21 on the board for a 24-6 halftime lead. They wound up with 252 yards on the ground, 21 yards above their average and quarterback JC French was able to throw for a career-best four touchdowns. We said JC French IV would make plays, but throw his first interception Outcome: His first interception was a pick-six by Peyton Morgan. Brice Pollock broke up a pass intended for Isaiah Johnson. There was originally a targeting call, which would have wiped away the touchdown, but it was reversed on review. On the next series, Amier Boyd picked off French. On the upside, French rebounded and added a fourth touchdown pass in the third quarter to Larenzo Fenner, to finish with four scoring passes in the game. Finally, we said if Texas Tech had momentum, they wouldn't go conservative Outcome: The Red Raiders lost momentum and therefore couldn't take retribution as billionaire donor Cody Campbell had insinuated . Instead, Campbell tweeted his displeasure with the loss after the game. There is no excuse or reason to lose a game like this. We have to be better. @TexasTechFB — Cody Campbell (@CodyC64) October 24, 2026 Overreactions from Cincinnati Bearcats vs. No. 8 Texas Tech Cincinnati Bearcats should be ranked Hit the brakes on that. UC is 5-2, a win away from bowl eligibility, but still has currently ranked teams ahead in the next two weeks, with Utah at home and a game in Houston. Utah improved to 8-0 with a a 21-13 home victory over now 6-2 Houston Saturday night. The Bearcats also have BYU in Provo Nov. 28. The Cougars will drop from No. 2 after getting knocked off by UCF in Orlando, 39-31 in overtime. But that's the two-time zone thing coming into play, just as it could again with UC traveling back to Mountain Time around Thanksgiving. The opportunity to be ranked is certainly there in the coming weeks. UC Bearcats defense is amazing! After Morgantown, fans were upset that the Bearcats shut down the No. 4 rushing offense on 134 yards, but allowed West Virginia quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. to throw for 464 yards in a 45-42 loss. Texas Tech came in averaging 38 points per game, with 192 yards on the ground and 230 yards through the air. The Bearcats held them to a season-low 24 points, 173 yards on the ground and 227 yards passing in the upset. Patrick Bauer had a pair of sacks, MJ Cannon had an interception and the Bearcats had seven tackles for loss. Until a garbage-time touchdown by Quinten Joyner in the final minute, UC gave up four field goals and Morgan's pick-six, which seemed controversial. UC defensive coordinator Nate Woody won this over former coaching colleague and Red Raiders defensive coordinator Shiel Wood, but one week doesn't make a season. Playing at home in Big 12 is an advantage Just as home field was insurmountable at Arizona and West Virginia, the 38,088 at Nippert Stadium made life difficult all day for quarterback Will Hammond and Texas Tech. Grades for Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Texas Tech Overall: A- It wasn't a wipeout, but UC led the game for 37 of the 60 minutes. Once they seized momentum in the second quarter with 21 unanswered points, the crowd and team were locked in. Offense: B French didn't have a 300-yard passing game, but he didn't need them. Going 19-for-30 for 172 yards was good enough to get him a personal-best four touchdown passes to Tabb, Malachi Henry, Lyviel Waters and Larenzo Fenner. Cole Tabb had a career-high 173 yards rushing with a touchdown catch and the first rushing touchdown allowed by Texas Tech this season. Defense: A- Texas Tech scored 52 points on Arizona State in its previous game and the Red Raiders' season-low was 28 at Colorado. J'Koby Williams had 165 yards rushing against Arizona State and was held to 81 by UC. MJ Cannon picked off Will Hammond and UC sacked him four times. Special Teams : B Max Fletcher averaged 43.5 yards per kick and pinned the Red Raiders inside the 20-yard line once. Stephen Rusnak connected on his lone 47-yard field goal, but the Bearcats had no punt or kick returns due to fair catches or touchbacks. Coaching: A- Give Scott Satterfield and Nate Woody credit as they took a lot of heat after losing a game late at West Virginia 45-42. Against Texas Tech, offense and defense contributed evenly. Also credit offensive line coach Nic Cardwell, who lost center Taran Tyo early in the game and replaced him with Grant Edgington, who didn't miss a beat. Utah makes their 1st visit to Nippert Stadium vs. Cincinnati Bearcats Ranked No. 10 this past week, Utah has never been to Nippert Stadium. Kickoff is at 3:45 p.m. A Halloween win would give the Bearcats a second straight Top 10 win and a bowl berth. The Utes beat Houston Saturday. item.title: Chiefs and 49ers suffer first losses of NFL season, Vikings stay unbeaten
item.description: Jessie Bates III of the Atlanta Falcons punches the ball out from George Kittle in the Falcons' NFL victory over the San Francisco 49ers (Todd Kirkland) The Seattle Seahawks put on a defensive masterclass to hand the Kansas City Chiefs their first defeat of the NFL season on Sunday, winning 20-3, while the San Francisco 49ers also surrendered their perfect start to the Atlanta Falcons. Seattle utterly stifled their former running back Kenneth Walker III, who won the Super Bowl last season with the Seahawks and had led the NFL this year with the Chiefs in rushing yards per game ahead of Sunday's clash. He could only manage 36 rushing yards from 14 carries on his return to Lumen Field, as the Seattle defense collectively swarmed their opponents, sacking Patrick Mahomes once and forcing another interception. "We just had the one mindset -- to go in and just disrupt," said Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori, who rushed Mahomes to create a Ty Okada pick that led to a Seattle touchdown on the next drive. The scoreline was the Chiefs' joint-lowest in a game Mahomes started. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught a looping 28-yard pass from Sam Darnold in the second quarter but was initially judged to have run out-of-bounds, before a video review awarded the touchdown. Walker's Seattle replacement Emanuel Wilson rushed 21 yards through a gap at the heart of the Chiefs' defense in the fourth quarter. Harrison Butker missed two field goals on a chastening night for the high-flying Chiefs. Meanwhile in Atlanta, Michael Penix threw for three touchdowns and the Falcons defense forced four turnovers in a 29-20 win over the 49ers. Penix connected with tight end Nick Muse for a touchdown to keep the Falcons within striking distance in the first half and hit Kyle Pitts for a TD that put Atlanta ahead in the third quarter. He found Drake London with a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth. "Too sloppy to win," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. - 'Proud' - Those results left the Minnesota Vikings as the only remaining unbeaten team, holding the Indianapolis Colts scoreless in the second half in a 16-10 victory that saw them improve to 6-0. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray threw a five-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter and Will Reichard kicked a 52-yard field goal with 1:39 remaining. Sunday's action kicked off in Paris, where Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers threw for 212 yards and a milestone touchdown to lead the Steelers to a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in the league's first regular-season game in the French capital. Rodgers hit Darnell Washington with a four-yard TD pass to give the Steelers a 10-3 lead late in the second quarter, his 540th regular-season touchdown pass moving him into solo third place on the all-time list ahead of Peyton Manning (539). Meanwhile in Atlanta, Michael Penix threw for three touchdowns and the Falcons defense forced four turnovers in a 29-20 win over the 49ers. Penix connected with tight end Nick Muse for a touchdown to keep the Falcons within striking distance in the first half and hit Kyle Pitts for a TD that put Atlanta ahead in the third quarter. He found Drake London with a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth. "Too sloppy to win," 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said. - 'Proud' - Those results left the Minnesota Vikings as the only remaining unbeaten team, holding the Indianapolis Colts scoreless in the second half in a 16-10 victory that saw them improve to 6-0. Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray threw a five-yard touchdown pass to T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter and Will Reichard kicked a 52-yard field goal with 1:39 remaining. Sunday's action kicked off in Paris, where Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers threw for 212 yards and a milestone touchdown to lead the Steelers to a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in the league's first regular-season game in the French capital. Rodgers hit Darnell Washington with a four-yard TD pass to give the Steelers a 10-3 lead late in the second quarter, his 540th regular-season touchdown pass moving him into solo third place on the all-time list ahead of Peyton Manning (539). The Los Angeles Rams snapped a two-game skid in emphatic style, beating the Raiders 35-21 in Las Vegas. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 195 yards and three touchdowns, all in the first half. He became the franchise leader in scoring passes -- an honor Stafford also holds with the Detroit Lions. "We've had some tough losses late in games this year, played good enough football to win games and hadn't gotten it done... proud of our resolve," said Stafford. In Houston, Devin Singletary ran 30 yards for a touchdown in overtime to lift the New York Giants to a 27-21 upset win over the Texans. In Detroit, Jake Bates kicked a 22-yard field goal as time expired to give the Lions a 20-17 victory over the Green Bay Packers. Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes in the second half as the Bengals rallied to beat the Ravens 35-13 in Baltimore. Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson piloted his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive of the season, capped by Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal as time expired in the Browns' 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans in Nashville. And the Miami Dolphins earned their first win of the season, beating the New York Jets 28-25 in New Jersey. amz-bb/lkd

item.title: Browns QB Deshaun Watson Backed for Major NFL Award
item.description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson quieted his critics. Getty Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 20: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns is taken off the field on a medical cart in the second quarter of a game against the Cincinnati Bengalsat Huntington Bank Field on October 20, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) Getty Deshaun Watson has gone from being booed by his home crowd to a candidate for a significant NFL honor. Watson — returning from two Achilles surgeries — has five game-winning drives for the 5-2 Cleveland Browns. Longtime team insider Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com believes Watson’s play has put him under consideration for Comeback Player of the Year, even with another prominent quarterback leading the race. “Deshaun Watson has gone from not knowing if he could ever play in front of Browns fans again to becoming a legitimate candidate for NFL Comeback Player of the Year,” Cabot said. “Of course, the Chiefs’ Patrick Mahomes is clearly the frontrunner for that coveted postseason award, but Watson, after pulling off his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive of the season in Sunday’s 27-24 victory over the Titans, has to at least be in the conversation.” Watson strengthened his case Sunday, throwing for 308 yards and delivering his fifth fourth-quarter game-winning drive in Cleveland’s 27-24 victory over the Tennessee Titans. The Browns improved to 5-2, with their quarterback producing his first 300-yard passing performance since joining the team. Mahomes, who is under center for the undefeated Chiefs , entered Sunday as a minus-175 favorite for the award, per DraftKings. Watson is in the mix, along with New York Giants receiver Malik Nabers, San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Wawner, and Jacksonville Jaguars second-year CB/WR Travis Hunter. Deshaun Watson Delivers Best Passing Day With Browns Getty Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers . Watson completed 25 of 36 passes against Tennessee, overcoming an early interception and adding a rushing touchdown. His 9-yard scoring run gave Cleveland a 24-17 lead with 4:34 remaining, but the Browns needed him again after Tony Pollard tied the game with 58 seconds left. Watson answered with a 36-yard completion to Harold Fannin Jr., putting Cleveland in position for Andre Szmyt’s winning 32-yard field goal as time expired. View this post on Instagram “He has something in him to be able to make plays when it counts,” Todd Monken said. “We’re trying to flatline our play earlier in the game to be more consistent.” Watson also received substantial help from Cleveland’s young supporting cast. Rookie receiver KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards, while Fannin finished with six receptions for 91 yards. Quinshon Judkins added 96 rushing yards and two touchdowns — by far his best game of the season.

Mahomes, who is under center for the undefeated Chiefs , entered Sunday as a minus-175 favorite for the award, per DraftKings. Watson is in the mix, along with New York Giants receiver Malik Nabers, San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Wawner, and Jacksonville Jaguars second-year CB/WR Travis Hunter. Deshaun Watson Delivers Best Passing Day With Browns Getty Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers . Watson completed 25 of 36 passes against Tennessee, overcoming an early interception and adding a rushing touchdown. His 9-yard scoring run gave Cleveland a 24-17 lead with 4:34 remaining, but the Browns needed him again after Tony Pollard tied the game with 58 seconds left. View this post on Instagram “He has something in him to be able to make plays when it counts,” Todd Monken said. “We’re trying to flatline our play earlier in the game to be more consistent.” Watson also received substantial help from Cleveland’s young supporting cast. Rookie receiver KC Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards, while Fannin finished with six receptions for 91 yards. Quinshon Judkins added 96 rushing yards and two touchdowns — by far his best game of the season. Watson Returns From Lengthy Injury Absence Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO – OCTOBER 20: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns is taken off the field on a medical cart in the second quarter of a game against the Cincinnati Bengalsat Huntington Bank Field on October 20, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) Watson’s award case begins with the injuries that kept him off the field. He ruptured his right Achilles tendon in October 2024 and required another operation after tearing it again. The Browns announced the second surgery in January 2025, leaving his return timetable uncertain. Despite returning to practice, he ultimately missed the entire 2025 season. The absence is relevant to the award’s criteria. The Associated Press’ guidance emphasizes overcoming injury, illness or other circumstances that caused a player to miss time the previous season. Joe Flacco was the last Browns player to win the award , earning the honor in 2023 after coming off the couch as an unsigned free agent and leading Cleveland to the playoffs. The AP clarified its guidance the following offseason, shifting the focus away from career revivals like Flacco’s and toward players overcoming injury, illness or similar adversity. item.title: Mike Brown gives the Knicks a reality check after their 0-3 start to the 2026-27 season
item.description: Mike Brown gives the Knicks a reality check after their 0-3 start to the 2026-27 season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the defending champions, the New York Knicks are struggling to start their title defense campaign because they are off to a slow 0-3 start. Heading into the 2026-27 NBA season, the Knicks were seen as the best team in the Eastern Conference by a lot of people, but they have not lived up to those expectations. It is still pretty early in the season, but losing the first three games of the season after a superb postseason run is not a good look. That is why Knicks head coach Mike Brown is demanding more from his players because he knows they are capable of so much more. Mike Brown is giving his Knicks team a reality check after a 0-3 start As the defending champions, expectations are high from both the wider NBA community and the people in the league. Teams want to beat the champions, and that has been clear because the Knicks have not won a game in their first three tries this season. To be fair to the Knicks, it has been a hard schedule playing against the Philadelphia 76ers , the Boston Celtics , and the Orlando Magic . However, the latest loss is a bit inexcusable because the Magic did not have Paolo Banchero, and they lost Jalen Suggs during the game. MORE: Mike Brown was unhappy with the Knicks after their loss to the 76ers It is not good to overreact to the slow start to the season, especially with what happened in the previous campaign. However, the Knicks eventually have to live up to the expectations because they are supposed to live up to the hype. Brown wants to see more fight from his team, as they should not be having struggles early on. "The biggest thing is to continue to coach them or tell them the truth. When we play well, as I told them just now, we were great in transition in the second half... If we're trying the right way, sometimes you go to fight through stuff like this to get back on track," Brown said about the Knicks' struggles to start the year . "Games like this will tell us that, as I said before, our crap stinks. It does, and we're the only ones that can do something about it. There's no light switch that we can just turn on and think we're going to win ball games. No one is going to give us anything." That is the kind of reality check that the Knicks need. They are the defending champions, so they have to live up to that billing. If they want to win another one, they have to be honest and work harder than everyone else. item.title: Thunder’s Mark Daigneault delivers sobering message after Jalen Williams injury
item.description: Credit: Rob Gray-USA TODAY Sports Thunder’s Mark Daigneault delivers sobering message after Jalen Williams injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Prior to sealing a 108-101 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers to move to 3-1 on the season, a devastating turn of events befell the Oklahoma City Thunder . With time winding down in the fourth quarter, All-Star forward Jalen Williams suffered a horrific ankle injury that the training staff immediately had to cover with a towel. The medical stuff then rushed to his aid, and he had to be stretchered off the floor. The early signs are not promising for the Thunder, and the players’ reaction during the immediate aftermath of Williams’ injury says it all. At the very least, it looks like a lengthy stint on the sidelines awaits the 25-year-old forward, putting OKC in such a tough position moving forward. “Those are tough, man,” Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault said in his postgame presser, via ClutchPoints beat reporter Josue Pavon. “We’re not doing great. That’s tough on the guys. Everyone empathizes. I think both teams, in those situations. So yeah, not doing great.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We’re not doing great. That’s tough on the guys. Everyone empathizes — both teams in those situations. So, yeah. Not doing great” Mark Daigneault on Jalen Williams’ gruesome leg injury. He added the Thunder will come in as a team tomorrow morning for an update on Williams pic.twitter.com/8KUfAfSHMw — Josue Pavón (@Joe_Sway) October 26, 2026 The fateful play happened with 1:14 remaining in the final frame. With the Thunder holding on to a precarious four-point lead, Williams made an aggressive play to drive to the basket, where he was met by Derrick Jones Jr. He then landed awkwardly and with brutal force on his ankle. According to a few experts on social media, it appears as though Williams had suffered an ankle dislocation and fracture. The Thunder, of course, will be waiting for the official diagnosis before it becomes clearer to them what his timeline for recovery will be. This is a tough development for Williams, who was raring to bounce back from an injury-riddled 2025-26 campaign. Last season, he only played in 33 regular-season games, and he missed four of the Thunder’s seven games against the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference Finals. Through three games this season, Williams has put up 13.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per contest. Related: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander keeps faith in Thunder despite Jalen Williams injury Related: Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton sends immediate message after Jalen Williams injury

According to a few experts on social media, it appears as though Williams had suffered an ankle dislocation and fracture. The Thunder, of course, will be waiting for the official diagnosis before it becomes clearer to them what his timeline for recovery will be. This is a tough development for Williams, who was raring to bounce back from an injury-riddled 2025-26 campaign. Last season, he only played in 33 regular-season games, and he missed four of the Thunder’s seven games against the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference Finals. Through three games this season, Williams has put up 13.7 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per contest. item.title: Is Petr Yan the UFC Bantamweight GOAT? Dana White Thinks So
item.description: UFC Dana White Petr Yan Getty Is UFC bantamweight champion Petr Yan the best to ever do it at 135 lbs? UFC president Dana White seems to think he is. Yan defeated Merab Dvalishvili in the pair’s trilogy bout in the main event of UFC 333 in what was one of the best fights of the year, with the pair winning $100,000 each for the Fight of the Night bonus. This is Yan’s second bantamweight title reign, and now, at age 32, he seems to be even better than ever. So, is he the best? White believes he is. Dana White Says Petr Yan Is the Best Bantamweight Ever Speaking to reporters post-UFC 333, White was asked if Yan is now the best bantamweight ever following his latest impressive victory inside the Octagon, and the UFC bossman said that he can’t disagree with that notion. “Yeah, it’d be tough to say no,” White said. Petr Yan UFC Resume Yan first entered the UFC in 2018 after having racked up an 8-1 record fighting in Russia. He immediately turned heads inside the Octagon, winning his first seven UFC fights, including a knockout win over Urijah Faber at UFC 245 in December 2019 and a TKO win over Jose Aldo at UFC 251 in July 2020 that saw him capture the vacant bantamweight title. Yan lost his belt in his first title defense when he was DQed against Aljamain Sterling at UFC 259 in March 2021. He bounced back against Cory Sandhagen in his next bout to claim the interim bantamweight title, but lost three straight fights after that, and it looked like he could be done as a top contender at that point. But Yan once again went on a long win streak, beating Song Yadong, Deiveson Figueiredo, and Marcus McGhee to earn a rematch with Dvalishvili, whom he beat at UFC 323 in December 2025 to claim the UFC bantamweight belt once again. Then, he successfully defended it against Dvalishvili in the pair’s epic trilogy bout at UFC 333. Overall, it’s hard to argue against Yan’s resume, and although Dominick Cruz has a real argument for the title of bantamweight GOAT, it does feel like Yan has surpassed him at this point. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Is Petr Yan the UFC Bantamweight GOAT? Dana White Thinks So appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard to undergo testing after concerning injury update
item.description: Brad Mills-Imagn Images Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard to undergo testing after concerning injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kawhi Leonard was missing in action on Sunday, as the Toronto Raptors lost to the Minnesota Timberwolves, 117-94, at Target Center. The Raptors fell to 2-1, while the Timberwolves improved to 3-0. Leonard was added to the injury report just an hour before tip-off. Toronto announced that the veteran forward was dealing with swelling in his left knee. He played 28 minutes in the Raptors’ win against the Washington Wizards on Friday, tallying 16 points on 7-of-20 shooting, nine rebounds, and three steals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) According to Yahoo! Canada’s Vivek Jacob, the 35-year-old Leonard will seek medical evaluation . “Darko Rajakovic says that Kawhi Leonard will undergo further testing for his left knee, and there will be an update after that. (His) status for Wednesday against the Orlando Magic is currently up in the air,” reported Jacob on X. The two-time Finals MVP is hoping to stay healthy after appearing in 65 games last season. He is also bullish on his much-needed reset with the Raptors after his controversy-filled departure from the Los Angeles Clippers. Leonard’s injury history is quite concerning, and the latest update is not exactly encouraging. But it is also likely that the Raptors are just being extra cautious with him. Ja’Kobe Walter replaced Leonard in the starting unit against Minnesota. He had 22 points, including 5-of-8 shooting from long distance, four rebounds, and two assists. RJ Barrett added 20 points and three steals, while Immanuel Quickley had 19 points and three rebounds. Scottie Barnes went scoreless on 0-of-12 shooting from the field. He had three assists and four steals. Related: Raptors’ Kawhi Leonard scratched from Timberwolves game with swelling in knee Related: Raptors’ Darko Rajakovic gives props to Toronto for tough team win over Wizards

item.title: Century King! Mbappe hits 100 Real Madrid goals with deadly double to sink Barcelona
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Kylian Mbappe reached a historic milestone by scoring his 100th goal for Real Madrid during a match-winning performance against Barcelona. The French forward insisted that squad unity mattered more than his personal benchmark. Mbappe hits century milestone in 116th appearance Kylian Mbappe etched his name further into Real Madrid history by scoring both goals in a 2-1 victory over Barcelona at the Camp Nou. The French striker reached 100 goals for Los Blancos in just his 116th appearance for the club. His century of goals includes 67 in La Liga, 25 in the Champions League, 4 in the Copa del Rey, 2 in the Club World Cup, 1 in the UEFA Super Cup, and 1 in the Spanish Super Cup. Mbappe opened the scoring via a deflected thigh effort before turning in Eduardo Camavinga's late assist. Striker puts team victory above personal benchmark Despite reaching three figures in record time, Mbappe remained completely focused on collective achievement post-match . "I'm very happy, everyone knows I like to score goals and help the team with that," Mbappe stated. "But I think today this is just a detail, because the most important thing is the team’s victory and how we win as a group." "This victory will give the group a lot of confidence and there will be many more goals, so it’s not that important," he added. Frenchman calls for absolute team unity in title pursuit Reflecting on the demands of playing for Real Madrid, Mbappe urged his team-mates to maintain their high standards. "We knew we had to play like men, but also as a team," Mbappe emphasized. "If we want to achieve things this year, we have to do them as a group... when you see the players we have here, anyone who says there isn't quality is a liar." "In the end, winning and still being in the title race is very important for us," he noted. Real Madrid striker sets sights on La Liga crown Having won two Pichichi Trophies and a Golden Boot since arriving in Madrid, Mbappe continues to anchor Los Blancos' attack. The Frenchman has already netted 14 goals across all competitions this season. Mbappe and Real Madrid turn their attention to next Sunday's away fixture against Santander.

With Tyreek Hill having still yet to sign with an NFL franchise despite his agent suggesting the former five-time All-Pro could join a team “with the next few days” back on Oct. 5; much of which could be due to a potentially impending suspension stemming from a civil court case in which Hill was found liable for two cases of battery earlier this month; KC may turn to other options. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Sid Lowe at the Camp Nou
item.content:encoded: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
item.description: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby. Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher. Continue reading...

item.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
item.description: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

item.title: Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian
item.description: Hibernian 1-2 Celtic; Rangers 4-0 St Johnstone Braga and Miller give Hearts 2-0 win at Motherwell Camilo Durán moved into double figures for the season as Celtic reasserted themselves at the top of the Premiership by coming from behind to defeat beleaguered Hibernian 2-1 at windy Easter Road. After another Europa League setback at home to Celta Vigo on Thursday, the champions bounced back with a victory that restored their four-point cushion over Rangers at the top. The home side, who are bottom, took an early lead through Owen Elding but it was swiftly cancelled out by a Jason Kerr own goal before Duran’s 10th of the season edged the visitors ahead just before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. Continue reading...

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.description: Lazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with Napoli Beier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht Frankfurt Lazio climbed to the top of Serie A with a 2-1 home win ⁠over Parma ⁠as Roma ​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw with Napoli in a pulsating clash in Naples. Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. Tottenham had a corner on the left-hand side, in a game that had felt to that point like an extended practice session, a refinement of systems, the football equivalent of watching two middle-aged men methodically emptying the dishwasher, adding salt, descaling the hoses, tutting over knives incorrectly slotted, cups in the wrong row. item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. Continue reading...

item.title: Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past Swansea
item.description: Hammers humbled at home; Swansea thrashed 5-0 Burnley sack manager Hayen after 4-1 loss at Lincoln Southampton announced themselves in the promotion race with a statement 3-2 win at the pre-season title favourites, West Ham . Kuryu Matsuki, James Bree and Lewis Dobbin were all on target in a chaotic first half, while Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers. Nuno Espírito Santo’s side would have gone top with a win but instead saw their nine-match unbeaten run halted. There were thousands of empty seats by the end at the London Stadium, with those who stayed booing the Hammers off. Southampton, deducted four points at the start of the season, are now just two points behind West Ham. Continue reading...

item.title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start
item.description: Defender costs three goals in past two league matches Emery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner Jackson Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, the Manchester City manager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season. Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villa a 2-1 victory at Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowed Ipswich to score twice against City last weekend. Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
item.description: Midfielder ‘who can never stand still’ has brought renewed energy to Seagulls since return to the club in January Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free.
